Case study / 01

Building Notifying.in from a simple event idea into a working product.

A 0→1 event discovery and notification platform for Indian users. The product connects event discovery, state-based relevance, web push, admin work, and ad management.

Visit Notifying.in ↗ Back to portfolio
My roleProduct Builder / Product & Business Analysis
Product stage0→1 and iterative product development
Core usersIndian users looking for important dates and reminders
FocusDiscovery, notifications, admin, monetisation
01 / Problem

The information was useful. Finding the right information was the real problem.

The product needed to make important days easy to understand and easy to remember, without forcing a user into a long account setup.

What had to work

People should be able to see upcoming festivals, holidays, dry days, fasting days and other important dates in one place.

The product also needed state-based relevance, a clear event structure, browser notifications, admin tools and a way to manage ads without changing the public site every time.

Event discovery State targeting Category logic Time-sensitive information Low-friction use
Product modelDate · State · Category
What matters next?
02 / Product system

I connected the pieces so each part could support the next.

The public experience, notification flow, admin tools and monetisation were built as connected parts of one product.

01

Organise the event data

Events were structured around dates, states and categories so the same information could power lists, event pages and notifications.

02

Keep the first-use path simple

The public product stays usable without login, and notification opt-in is presented as a clear value-based action.

03

Make notifications manageable

A web-push flow, custom notification composer and notification logs turn sending into a visible product workflow rather than a hidden technical task.

04

Give the admin a clear control layer

Events, targeting, activation, visits, users and device information are available from dedicated admin screens.

05

Make ads configurable

Ad type, placement, targeting, dates, priority and status can be managed without hard-coding each campaign into the public page.

03 / Product in practice

The screenshots show the product from the user side and the admin side.

Each screen below is included because it shows a real product decision, workflow or operating tool.

Public homepage

Make the main value clear in the first view.

The homepage puts the next important day, search, preferences and notification value in one place. The goal is to make the product understandable before a user needs to explore deeper.

Public experience

Make relevance visible.

State filtering and clear event labels help a user understand which dates matter to them.

Mobile experience

Keep the important action easy to reach.

The mobile screens keep the core message and notification action visible without adding extra steps.

Admin control

Give the product an operating layer.

The admin side is designed to manage content, delivery and day-to-day product changes.

Admin dashboard

One place to see what is happening.

The dashboard brings events, notifications, delivery rate, website visits, users and device status into one control view.

What this shows The product does not stop at the public page. It also needs clear screens for creating content, sending notifications and checking what happened afterward.
Notification workflow

Compose → preview → target → send.

The notification flow makes the action easy to understand and gives the admin a view of the audience before sending.

Custom notification composer

See the message and the audience before sending.

The composer combines the title, body, icon, large image and link with a live notification preview and audience/device counts.

Ad system

Build monetisation as something the admin can manage.

These screens show the ad system from high-level control to inventory and the step-by-step creation flow.

Ad Manager

Keep ad settings in one place.

The Ad Manager brings managed ad counts, status and Google AdSense Auto Ads settings together in one screen.

Product decision Instead of treating advertising as one hard-coded block, the product separates type, placement, schedule, targeting, priority and status. That makes future changes easier to manage.
Architecture

Technology supported the product model.

The implementation combines front-end pages, PHP/MySQL data handling, a Node.js/Express notification service using Web Push, service-worker support and a WordPress layer for future content growth.

HTML / CSS / JSPHP / MySQLNode.js / ExpressWeb PushWordPress
Product execution

Scope was built in clear phases.

The work moved through event management, notification history, custom sends and ad management. The next planned layers are stronger search discovery, automated notifications and a focused content layer.

RequirementsProduct logicJiraScrumPRD thinking
Snapshot from the supplied admin screenshots The dashboard and notification-log captures show 11 notifications, 193 successful deliveries, a 93.2% delivery rate and 27 users at the time of capture. These are screenshot values, not lifetime product claims.

“A notification feature is only useful when the data is clear, the user understands the value, the send is reliable, and the admin can see what happened.”
